title: No Perfect Guardrail & No Perfect Guard: On the Decidability of Output Policies for Large Language Models
abstract: arXiv:2611.27260v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Expecting guardrails to provide a general guarantee of safety fails to recognize the limits of computational enforcement and policy specification. We argue that promising such perfection is an ethical failure of precision, and that invoking it to abdicate responsibility is a moral failure. Guardrails can support responsible action, but cannot relieve researchers, developers, policymakers, or users of their obligations to examine what they claim, permit, and prevent.   We establish a precise computational boundary. If every finite string is a possible output of a language model, a computable guard that blocks every forbidden output and passes every permitted one exists if and only if the policy is decidable. For an undecidable policy, every guard misclassifies infinitely many strings, and every guard that blocks all forbidden outputs excludes infinitely many permitted ones. translated_title: 没有完美的护栏，也没有完美的守卫：论大语言模型输出策略的可判定性
translated_abstract: 期待护栏能够提供普遍的安全性保证，未能认识到计算执行与策略规范本身的局限。我们认为，承诺这种完美是一种精准度上的伦理失败，而援引这种完美来推卸责任则是一种道德失败。护栏可以支持负责任的行动，但无法免除研究人员、开发者、政策制定者或用户审视其所主张、允许和阻止之内容的义务。我们确立了一个精确的计算边界：如果每个有限字符串都是语言模型可能的输出，那么一个能够阻止所有被禁止输出并放行所有被允许输出的可计算守卫，当且仅当该策略是可判定的时候才存在。对于一个不可判定的策略，每个守卫都会错误分类无穷多个字符串，而每个阻止了所有被禁止输出的守卫都必然排除无穷多个被允许的输出。我们将这一刻画应用于算术真理、程序行为等领域。
tldr: 本文利用可计算性理论证明：只有当大语言模型的输出策略可判定时，才存在能完美区分禁止与允许输出的可计算护栏；对于不可判定的策略，任何护栏都必然误分类无穷多字符串，因此护栏不能免除人类自身的审查与责任。
en_tdlr: Using computability theory, this paper proves that a computable guard perfectly enforcing an LLM output policy exists if and only if the policy is decidable—for undecidable policies, every guard misclassifies infinitely many strings, so guardrails cannot absolve humans of their responsibility.
